Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G
A
In December of 1869, Congress appointed a commission to select a site and prepare plans and cost estimates for a new State Department Building. Later, the commission was also charged with finding a site and planning for a new War and Navy Department Building.
1869年12月，国会任命一个委员会，为新国务院大楼选址并拟定方案与费用估算。后来，该委员会还受命为新的陆军暨海军部大楼选址并作规划。
B
Completed in 1875, the State Department's south wing was the first to be occupied, with its elegant four-story library (completed in 1876), Cabinet Room, and Secretary's office.
国务院大楼南翼于1875年落成并率先启用，内有典雅的四层图书馆（1876年竣工）、内阁会议室和国务卿办公室。
C
The State, War, and Navy Building, as it was originally known, housed the three Executive Branch Departments most intimately connected with formulating foreign policy and the making of war and peace. It was where many of the most celebrated national figures of the nation's history made their mark.
这座建筑最初名为国务院、陆军部与海军部大楼，容纳了与制定外交政策和决定战争与和平关系最为密切的三个行政部门。国家历史上许多最负盛名的显要人物，都曾在此留下印记。
D
Many of the most celebrated national figures have participated in historical events that have taken place within the EEOB's granite walls. Theodore and Franklin D. Roosevelt, William Howard Taft, Dwight D. Eisenhower, and a host of other American presidents and foreign dignitaries have walked its corridors.
众多最负盛名的国家人物都曾参与发生在EEOB花岗岩墙壁之内的历史事件。西奥多·罗斯福、富兰克林·D·罗斯福、威廉·霍华德·塔夫脱、德怀特·D·艾森豪威尔，以及众多其他美国总统与外国政要，都曾走过它的走廊。
E
The Eisenhower Executive Office Building (EEOB) commands a unique position in both the national history and the architectural heritage of the United States. Built from 1871 to 1888, its colorful history and vast, gracefully ornate interior have inspired numerous books, films, and even a song.
艾森豪威尔行政办公楼（EEOB）在美国国家历史与建筑遗产中都占据着独特地位。它建于1871至1888年间，其多姿的历史与广阔而优雅华美的内饰，激发了无数书籍、电影甚至一首歌曲的灵感。
F
Construction took 17 years as the building slowly rose wing by wing. When the EEOB was finished, it was the largest office building in Washington, with nearly two miles of black and white tiled corridors. Its interior was designed with state-of-the-art technology of the day, including fireproofing, electric light, and its own telephone system.
建筑耗时17年，以一翼一翼缓慢拔地而起。EEOB落成时是华盛顿最大的办公建筑，拥有近两英里黑白瓷砖铺就的走廊。其内部采用了当时的尖端技术，包括防火、电灯以及独立的电话系统。
G
The history of the EEOB began long before its foundations were laid. The first executive offices were constructed between 1799 and 1820, and the State Department was located in them. The building's early history was marked by frequent relocation and expansion as the young republic grew.
EEOB的历史远在其奠基之前就已开始。最早的行政办公室建于1799至1820年间，国务院便设于此。随着年轻共和国的成长，这座建筑的早期历史以频繁迁址与扩张为标志。

source_blocks.html:
参考范文

As is vividly shown in the cartoon, a student hesitates before the course-selection system, caught between two tempting options: courses that are new, innovation-oriented and challenging, and courses that promise high grades, easy credits and little homework.

The drawing conveys a thought-provoking message: course selection mirrors a student's underlying attitude toward learning. Driven by utilitarian concerns, some undergraduates shy away from demanding courses and chase easy credits. While such a strategy may inflate their GPA, it deprives them of the very knowledge and creativity that higher education is meant to cultivate. Real growth rarely comes from the path of least resistance.

From my perspective, university students should prioritize courses that stretch their abilities over those that merely pad their transcripts. After all, it is solid competence, not a glossy report card, that secures one's future in an increasingly competitive world.

【译文】

如漫画生动所示，一名学生在选课系统前犹豫不决，徘徊于两种诱人的选项之间：一类课程新颖、重创新、有难度；另一类则承诺高分、易通过、作业少。

这幅画传达了发人深省的道理：选课折射出学生对学习的根本态度。受功利心驱使，一些大学生回避有挑战的课程、追逐容易拿到的学分。这种策略虽能抬高绩点，却使他们错失了高等教育本应培养的知识与创造力。真正的成长很少来自最省力的那条路。

在我看来，大学生应优先选择能拓展能力的课程，而非仅为装点成绩单的课程。毕竟，在这个日益竞争的世界里，真正保障未来的，是扎实的能力，而非光鲜的成绩单。

Lower-income jobs like gardening or day care don't appeal to robots. But many middle-class occupations—trucking, financial advice, software engineering—have aroused their interest, or soon will. The rich own the robots, so they will be fine.

This isn't to be alarmist. Optimists point out that technological upheaval has benefited workers in the past. The Industrial Revolution didn't go so well for Luddites whose jobs were displaced by mechanized looms, but it eventually raised living standards and created more jobs than it destroyed. Likewise, automation should eventually boost productivity, stimulate demand by driving down prices, and free workers from hard, boring work. But in the medium term, middle-class workers may need a lot of help adjusting.

The first step, as Erik Brynjolfsson and Andrew McAfee argue in The Second Machine Age, should be rethinking education and job training. Curriculums—from grammar school to college—should evolve to focus less on memorizing facts and more on creativity and complex communication. Vocational schools should do a better job of fostering problem-solving skills and helping students work alongside robots. Online education can supplement the traditional kind. It could make extra training and instruction affordable. Professionals trying to acquire new skills will be able to do so without going into debt.

The challenge of coping with automation underlines the need for the U.S. to revive its fading business dynamism: Starting new companies must be made easier. In previous eras of drastic technological change, entrepreneurs smoothed the transition by dreaming up ways to combine labor and machines. The best uses of 3D printers and virtual reality haven't been invented yet. The U.S. needs the new companies that will invent them.

Finally, because automation threatens to widen the gap between capital income and labor income, taxes and the safety net will have to be rethought. Taxes on low-wage labor need to be cut, and wage subsidies such as the earned income tax credit should be expanded: This would boost incomes, encourage work, reward companies for job creation, and reduce inequality.

最后，由于自动化有可能拉大资本收入与劳动收入之间的差距，税收和社会保障体系将不得不重新考量。对低工资劳动的征税需要削减，劳动所得税抵免等工资补贴应扩大：这将提高收入、鼓励就业、奖励创造岗位的企业，并减少不平等。

Technology will improve society in ways big and small over the next few years, yet this will be little comfort to those who find their lives and careers upended by automation. Destroying the machines that are coming for our jobs would be nuts. But policies to help workers adapt will be indispensable.

未来几年，技术将以大大小小的方式改善社会，但对那些生活和职业被自动化颠覆的人来说，这算不上安慰。毁掉来抢饭碗的机器是疯了。但帮助劳动者适应的政策不可或缺。

paragraphs.html: Any fair-minded assessment of the dangers of the deal between Britain's National Health Service (NHS) and DeepMind must start by acknowledging that both sides mean well. DeepMind is one of the leading artificial intelligence (AI) companies in the world. The potential of this work applied to healthcare is very great, but it could also lead to further concentration of power in the tech giants. It is against that background that the information commissioner, Elizabeth Denham, has issued her damning verdict against the Royal Free hospital trust under the NHS, which handed over to DeepMind the records of 1.6 million patients in 2015 on the basis of a vague agreement which took far too little account of the patients' rights and their expectations of privacy.

paragraphs.html: 对英国国民医疗服务体系（NHS）与DeepMind之间协议的风险，任何公正的评估都必须首先承认双方本意都不坏。DeepMind是全球领先的人工智能公司之一。这项工作应用于医疗的潜力巨大，但也可能导致权力进一步集中在科技巨头手中。正是在这一背景下，信息专员伊丽莎白·德纳姆对NHS旗下的皇家 free 医院信托开出了谴责性裁决：该信托于2015年依据一份含糊的协议将160万患者的记录交给了DeepMind，而该协议几乎没有顾及患者的权利和他们对隐私的期望。

paragraphs.html: DeepMind has almost apologised. The NHS trust has mended its ways. Further arrangements—and there may be many—between the NHS and DeepMind will be carefully scrutinised to ensure that all necessary permissions have been asked of patients and all unnecessary data has been cleaned. There are lessons about informed patient consent to learn. But privacy is not the only angle in this case and not even the most important. Ms Denham chose to concentrate the blame on the NHS trust, since under existing law it "controlled" the data and DeepMind merely "processed" it. But this distinction misses the point that it is processing and aggregation, not the mere possession of bits, that gives the data value.

Any fair-minded assessment of the dangers of the deal between Britain's National Health Service (NHS) and DeepMind must start by acknowledging that both sides mean well. DeepMind is one of the leading artificial intelligence (AI) companies in the world. The potential of this work applied to healthcare is very great, but it could also lead to further concentration of power in the tech giants. It is against that background that the information commissioner, Elizabeth Denham, has issued her damning verdict against the Royal Free hospital trust under the NHS, which handed over to DeepMind the records of 1.6 million patients in 2015 on the basis of a vague agreement which took far too little account of the patients' rights and their expectations of privacy.

对英国国民医疗服务体系（NHS）与DeepMind之间协议的风险，任何公正的评估都必须首先承认双方本意都不坏。DeepMind是全球领先的人工智能公司之一。这项工作应用于医疗的潜力巨大，但也可能导致权力进一步集中在科技巨头手中。正是在这一背景下，信息专员伊丽莎白·德纳姆对NHS旗下的皇家 free 医院信托开出了谴责性裁决：该信托于2015年依据一份含糊的协议将160万患者的记录交给了DeepMind，而该协议几乎没有顾及患者的权利和他们对隐私的期望。

DeepMind has almost apologised. The NHS trust has mended its ways. Further arrangements—and there may be many—between the NHS and DeepMind will be carefully scrutinised to ensure that all necessary permissions have been asked of patients and all unnecessary data has been cleaned. There are lessons about informed patient consent to learn. But privacy is not the only angle in this case and not even the most important. Ms Denham chose to concentrate the blame on the NHS trust, since under existing law it "controlled" the data and DeepMind merely "processed" it. But this distinction misses the point that it is processing and aggregation, not the mere possession of bits, that gives the data value.

DeepMind几乎已经道歉。NHS信托也已改正做法。NHS与DeepMind之间进一步的安排（可能会有很多）将受到仔细审查，以确保已向患者征得一切必要许可、所有不必要的数据已被清除。在患者知情同意方面有教训可吸取。但隐私并非此案的唯一角度，甚至不是最重要的角度。德纳姆选择把责任集中在NHS信托身上，因为根据现行法律，是它"控制"数据，而DeepMind仅仅"处理"数据。但这一区分没有抓住要点：赋予数据价值的，正是处理和聚合，而非单纯地占有这些比特。

The great question is who should benefit from the analysis of all the data that our lives now generate. Privacy law builds on the concept of damage to an individual from identifiable knowledge about them. That misses the way the surveillance economy works. The data of an individual there gains its value only when it is compared with the data of countless millions more.

即便通过众议院，这项措施仍须过参议院——在那里必定有人会指出，它不过是维持邮政局运转的最最底线，远非全面改革。USPS的集体谈判没有任何改变，考虑到人员成本占该局开支的80%，这是重大疏漏。同样被忽略的还有取消周六信件投递的讨论。这一合乎常理的改动拥有广泛公众支持，每年可为USPS节省20亿美元。但邮政特殊利益集团似乎已将其扼杀，至少在众议院如此。围绕该法案达成的初步共识表明，议员们开始害怕USPS出现政治上难堪的短期崩溃。然而，这并不意味着他们正认真对待面向21世纪的邮政体系转型。
passages.text: The U.S. Postal Service (USPS) continues to bleed red ink. It reported a net loss of $5.6 billion for fiscal 2016, the 10th straight year its expenses have exceeded revenue. Meanwhile, it has more than $120 billion in unfunded liabilities, mostly for employee health and retirement costs. There are many reasons this formerly stable federal institution finds itself on the verge of bankruptcy. Fundamentally, the USPS is in a historic squeeze between technological change that has permanently decreased demand for its bread-and-butter product, first-class mail, and a regulatory structure that denies management the flexibility to adjust its operations to the new reality. 美国邮政（USPS）持续亏损。它公布2016财年净亏损56亿美元，这是其开支连续第10年超过收入。与此同时，它还有超过1200亿美元无着落的负债，主要用于员工健康和退休成本。这个昔日稳定的联邦机构陷入破产边缘，原因有很多。从根本上说，USPS处在一场历史性挤压之中：一头是技术变革永久降低了对其核心产品——一类邮件——的需求；另一头是监管结构剥夺了管理层根据新现实调整运营的灵活性。 And interest groups ranging from postal unions to greeting-card makers exert self-interested pressure on the USPS's ultimate overseer—Congress—insisting that whatever else happens to the Postal Service, aspects of the status quo they depend on get protected. This is why repeated attempts at reform legislation have failed in recent years, leaving the Postal Service unable to pay its bills except by deferring vital modernization. 而从邮政工会到贺卡制造商等各类利益集团，都向USPS的最终监管者——国会——施加自利性压力，坚持无论邮政局其他方面如何变化，他们所依赖的现状必须得到保护。这就是近年来改革立法一再失败的原因，结果是邮政局除了推迟至关重要的现代化之外，无力支付账单。 Now comes word that everyone involved—Democrats, Republicans, the Postal Service, the unions and the system's heaviest users—has finally agreed on a plan to fix the system. Legislation is moving through the House that would save USPS an estimated $28.6 billion over five years, which could help pay for new vehicles, among other survival measures. Most of the money would come from a penny-per-letter permanent rate increase and from shifting postal retirees into Medicare. The latter step would largely offset the financial burden of annually pre-funding retiree health care, thus addressing a long-standing complaint by the USPS and its unions. 现在有消息称，所有相关方——民主党、共和党、邮政局、工会以及该体系的重度用户——终于就一项修复方案达成一致。一项立法正在众议院推进，预计五年内可为USPS节省约286亿美元，可用于支付新车辆等生存措施。资金大部分来自每封信永久涨价1美分，以及将邮政退休人员转入联邦医保。后一项措施将在很大程度上抵消每年预付退休人员医疗保健的财政负担，从而解决USPS及其工会长期以来的抱怨。 If it clears the House, this measure would still have to get through the Senate—where someone is bound to point out that it amounts to the bare, bare minimum necessary to keep the Postal Service afloat, not comprehensive reform. There's no change to collective bargaining at the USPS, a major omission considering that personnel accounts for 80 percent of the agency's costs. Also missing is any discussion of eliminating Saturday letter delivery. That common-sense change enjoys wide public support and would save the USPS $2 billion per year. But postal special-interest groups seem to have killed it, at least in the House. partb_options.head: Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G

options.label: A
options.en: In December of 1869, Congress appointed a commission to select a site and prepare plans and cost estimates for a new State Department Building. Later, the commission was also charged with finding a site and planning for a new War and Navy Department Building.
options.zh: 1869年12月，国会任命一个委员会，为新国务院大楼选址并拟定方案与费用估算。后来，该委员会还受命为新的陆军暨海军部大楼选址并作规划。

options.label: B
options.en: Completed in 1875, the State Department's south wing was the first to be occupied, with its elegant four-story library (completed in 1876), Cabinet Room, and Secretary's office.
options.zh: 国务院大楼南翼于1875年落成并率先启用，内有典雅的四层图书馆（1876年竣工）、内阁会议室和国务卿办公室。

options.label: C
options.en: The State, War, and Navy Building, as it was originally known, housed the three Executive Branch Departments most intimately connected with formulating foreign policy and the making of war and peace. It was where many of the most celebrated national figures of the nation's history made their mark.
options.zh: 这座建筑最初名为国务院、陆军部与海军部大楼，容纳了与制定外交政策和决定战争与和平关系最为密切的三个行政部门。国家历史上许多最负盛名的显要人物，都曾在此留下印记。

options.label: D
options.en: Many of the most celebrated national figures have participated in historical events that have taken place within the EEOB's granite walls. Theodore and Franklin D. Roosevelt, William Howard Taft, Dwight D. Eisenhower, and a host of other American presidents and foreign dignitaries have walked its corridors.
options.zh: 众多最负盛名的国家人物都曾参与发生在EEOB花岗岩墙壁之内的历史事件。西奥多·罗斯福、富兰克林·D·罗斯福、威廉·霍华德·塔夫脱、德怀特·D·艾森豪威尔，以及众多其他美国总统与外国政要，都曾走过它的走廊。

options.label: E
options.en: The Eisenhower Executive Office Building (EEOB) commands a unique position in both the national history and the architectural heritage of the United States. Built from 1871 to 1888, its colorful history and vast, gracefully ornate interior have inspired numerous books, films, and even a song.
options.zh: 艾森豪威尔行政办公楼（EEOB）在美国国家历史与建筑遗产中都占据着独特地位。它建于1871至1888年间，其多姿的历史与广阔而优雅华美的内饰，激发了无数书籍、电影甚至一首歌曲的灵感。

options.label: F
options.en: Construction took 17 years as the building slowly rose wing by wing. When the EEOB was finished, it was the largest office building in Washington, with nearly two miles of black and white tiled corridors. Its interior was designed with state-of-the-art technology of the day, including fireproofing, electric light, and its own telephone system.
options.zh: 建筑耗时17年，以一翼一翼缓慢拔地而起。EEOB落成时是华盛顿最大的办公建筑，拥有近两英里黑白瓷砖铺就的走廊。其内部采用了当时的尖端技术，包括防火、电灯以及独立的电话系统。

options.label: G
options.en: The history of the EEOB began long before its foundations were laid. The first executive offices were constructed between 1799 and 1820, and the State Department was located in them. The building's early history was marked by frequent relocation and expansion as the young republic grew.
options.zh: EEOB的历史远在其奠基之前就已开始。最早的行政办公室建于1799至1820年间，国务院便设于此。随着年轻共和国的成长，这座建筑的早期历史以频繁迁址与扩张为标志。
